rules.justification: Fast mode of the Eigen SparseLU translation against its bitwise default (D-122, D-123): the panel products, the triangular panel solves and the GEMV kernels round each term c + a*b once (fused multiply-add) instead of twice. Each factor entry is a sum of at most a supernode width (128) of such terms, so it changes by at most about 128 units of 2^-53 relative to the sum of its terms' magnitudes, the order of the rounding error of the bitwise factorisation itself; the solution then changes by about kappa(A) times that relative to max|x|. The test matrix is a diagonally dominant unsymmetric 3-D 7-point stencil (Gershgorin: eigenvalues in [0.5, 13.4], kappa about 27), so the expected difference is of order 1e-14 of max|x|; the bound 1e-12 of max|x| covers longer sums and a pivot choice near a tie, and fails on a kernel error, which changes the solution at the 1e-3 level or more.
rules.evidence: akantu-linalg tests/fast_mode_sparse_lu.rs, 16^3 stencil (4096 unknowns), AMD EPYC 9B14 (AVX-512 + FMA instances), 2026-11-17: largest |fast - bitwise| / max|bitwise| 3.8e-16 (ratio to the bound 3.8e-4), 3268 of 4096 entries bit-identical (after the one-column product of the column updates went back to the bitwise kernel; 3265 before); identical at 2 and 4 threads (finest grain). On CPUs without an FMA instance (aarch64 NEON, x86-64 below AVX2) the fast mode runs the bitwise kernels and the two runs are identical.

rules.justification: Nested dissection against COLAMD in the Eigen SparseLU translation (D-122, D-125): the columns are eliminated in another order, so every factor entry is another sum of rounded products and the threshold pivoting may choose other rows. Both factorisations are backward stable with backward errors of order u = 2^-53 times the growth factor, so the two solutions differ by about kappa(A) times those backward errors, relative to max|x|. The test's matrices are a 3-D grid with 3 unknowns per node (3,000 unknowns), one with 1 unknown per node (4,096) and a saddle-point matrix (2,160) that pivots off the diagonal in about half of its columns with both orderings, all of moderate conditioning: the expected difference is of order 1e-15 of max|x|. The bound 1e-12 of max|x| leaves room for longer elimination paths and for a pivot choice near a tie, and fails on an ordering error (a permutation applied wrongly changes the solution at the 1e-1 level or more). Problems of larger condition number differ more, in proportion (evidence).
rules.evidence: akantu-linalg tests/sparse_lu_ordering.rs, AMD EPYC 9B14, 2026-11-17: largest |ND - COLAMD| / max|COLAMD| 2.1e-15 (ratio to the bound 2.1e-3), 122 to 217 entries per matrix bit-identical, residuals ||Ax - b|| / ||b|| of both orderings 6.5e-16 to 2.4e-15; the same on Apple M-series (NEON). Benchmark suite, size m, every solver case (docs/benchmarks/perf-campaign/sparselu-nd/diag/summary.md, diagnostic build): the digested states of the two orderings differ by 1.4e-17 to 3.5e-13 of their largest value on 13 cases with 1-norm condition estimates 1e2 to 2.5e11, and by 4.8e-12 on the DKT18 plate (condition estimate 1.8e10, off-diagonal pivots in 45 % of the columns, residuals 6.6e-11 and 1.3e-10); residuals of the two orderings of the same size on every case. Cohesive static solve, h = 0.12 (14,472 unknowns): potential and kinetic energies after 10 explicit steps differ by 6e-16 and 5e-13 relatively (docs/benchmarks/perf-campaign/sparselu-nd/README.md, Validation).
